headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no shared write channel is documented, but Rasa’s networked support-bot outputs can still be misused if wired to LightZero outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no documented input channel or filesystem/MCP bridge, so it cannot directly ingest Rasa output by default. Rasa does expose chat channels and can relay text to users, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser path. The only plausible bridge is manual or custom integration, so the injection pathway is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator wires LightZero outputs into a Rasa intent or message parser
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except through human review
Disable any automatic parsing of LightZero text by Rasa
Use a one-way export format with no executable markup
Add a manual approval step before Rasa forwards any LightZero-derived content

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero is documented with no filesystem read/write and no network egress, while Rasa has allowlisted egress and handles text/voice through external channels. There is no documented shared workspace or secret-bearing data class overlap, so leakage is not default. Risk remains if operators route sensitive text from Rasa into LightZero logs or prompts via custom glue.
conditions: IF sensitive customer text from Rasa is copied into LightZero prompts or logs
IF a shared workspace is introduced that both agents can read
mitigations: Avoid placing customer data in shared files
Strip identifiers before passing text between systems
Keep LightZero offline and isolated from support transcripts
Review any integration for secret propagation before enabling it

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it has no documented mutable-resource overlap with Rasa. Rasa supports multiple instances false and has allowlisted egress, but no shared write surface is documented. Without overlapping write authority, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locking-free git operations
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared assets
Do not mount a common writable directory
If shared state is needed, add explicit locking
Separate deployment credentials and runtime identities

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can turn upstream text into user-facing dialogue, so if LightZero outputs are fed into Rasa without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect support responses. LightZero is a game-playing system with no documented validation or factuality controls, and Rasa’s dialogue handling can present content authoritatively. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF LightZero-generated text is used as an input to Rasa responses
IF Rasa forwards LightZero output without a human or rule-based verification step
mitigations: Require human review of any LightZero-derived content
Add a validation layer before Rasa sends messages
Restrict Rasa to templated responses only
Log and sample-check downstream outputs for hallucinated facts

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated handling is documented for either agent. LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress; Rasa touches text and voice but no PHI, EU PII, or retention policy is specified. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent from the profiles, no compliance breach pathway is established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is later routed through Rasa
IF retention or residency policies are configured to conflict
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair
Document retention and residency settings before deployment
Add data-class filtering at ingress
Review vendor compliance terms before enabling sensitive workloads
